fatti.affermazione: John Backus gave the 1977 Turing Award lecture, «Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style? A Functional Style and Its Algebra of Programs» (Communications of the ACM 21(8), August 1978, pp. 613–641). In it he called conventional languages «von Neumann languages», coined «von Neumann bottleneck» and proposed the functional language FP.
fatti.fonte: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/359576.359579 (cited from memory: no online check was possible this round)

fatti.affermazione: Alan Perlis, the first Turing Award winner (1966), epigram 19: «A language that doesn't affect the way you think about programming, is not worth knowing», in Epigrams on Programming, ACM SIGPLAN Notices 17(9), September 1982. My Italian translation: «Un linguaggio che non influisce sul tuo modo di pensare la programmazione non vale la pena di conoscerlo».
fatti.fonte: https://www.cs.yale.edu/homes/perlis-alan/quotes.html (the fetch failed: the proxy blocked the host; to re-check)

fatti.affermazione: Lua means «moon» in Portuguese. At Tecgraf (PUC-Rio, Rio de Janeiro) its authors had already made a language called SOL (Simple Object Language), and «sol» means «sun».
fatti.fonte: https://www.lua.org/history.html and «The Evolution of Lua», HOPL III 2007 (the fetch failed: host blocked; to re-check)

fatti.affermazione: Kernighan's original B hello world: the constants 'hell', 'o, w' and 'orld' printed with putchar, because each constant held at most 4 characters. Dated 1972 in the lab.
TypeScript, JavaScript with types, was presented by Microsoft in October 2012, with Anders Hejlsberg among its designers.
fatti.fonte: general knowledge, matching the lab data; not re-checked online this round

fatti.affermazione: The map holds 58 languages and 93 influences. The most prolific ancestor in the map is FORTRAN: 42 of the 58 languages descend from it, directly or indirectly.
